title: Relaxed Weekend Beanie
summary: A slouchy seed-stitch beanie with a deep, fold-up 2 × 2 ribbed brim and a smooth shaped crown. Sized for your 56 cm head, this is an intermediate first project because it introduces purling, circular knitting and crown shaping.
what_i_saw: You described a relaxed weekend beanie with a deep 2 × 2 ribbed brim and a seed-stitch body; no photo or colour was supplied.
assumptions: The deep brim is folded up, not worn as a single layer.
A single solid colour and a smooth knit crown are acceptable; the slouch comes primarily from extra length.
The stitch count uses your recorded gauge of 18 stitches per 10 cm; check that you can match it in seed stitch in the round.
The nominal body circumference at that gauge is about 51.1 cm, before allowing for the fabric stretching around your 56 cm head. The rib will draw in when relaxed.

yarn.weight: Medium-weight yarn suitable for 5 mm needles and the stated gauge
yarn.amount: About 220–250 m; buy enough of the same dye lot
colours: Oatmeal, or one solid colour of your choice
yarn.note: A smooth, springy yarn makes the rib and seed texture easier to see. Check the care instructions on the ball band.

tools.name: Circular knitting needle
tools.why: For the brim and body in the round.

tools.name: Double-pointed needles
tools.size_or_qty: 5 mm, a set of 4 or 5, about 15–20 cm long
tools.why: For the crown once it becomes too small for the circular needle.

tools.name: Stitch marker
tools.why: To mark the beginning of each round.

tools.name: Blunt yarn needle
tools.why: To gather the crown and weave in the tails.

tools.name: Tape measure
tools.why: To check gauge, fit and section lengths.

skills.why: Choose yarn and follow its care instructions.

skills.why: Make the stretchy lower edge of the brim.

skills.name: The knit stitch
skills.why: Make knit stitches in the brim, body and crown.

skills.why: Make the hat as a seamless tube.

new_lessons.title: Seed stitch in the round
new_lessons.goal: Make an even pebbly fabric by alternating knit and purl stitches over an even number of stitches.
steps: Place a marker at the start of the round. Hold the needle with the next stitch in your left hand and the working needle and yarn in your right hand.
For the first round, bring the yarn between the needle tips to the front and purl one stitch.
Move the yarn between the tips to the back and knit one stitch. Repeat purl one, knit one to the marker.
For the next round, keep the yarn at the back and knit the first stitch.
Bring the yarn between the tips to the front and purl the next stitch. Repeat knit one, purl one to the marker.
Repeat these two rounds, knitting the purl bumps and purling the knit Vs from the round below.
new_lessons.check: The fabric has small scattered bumps rather than vertical columns, and the stitch count stays the same.
new_lessons.watch: If you get rib-like columns, you may be repeating the same round instead of alternating the two rounds; check the stitches below and knit a bump or purl a V.

new_lessons.title: Gather the live crown stitches
new_lessons.goal: Close the top of the hat securely through the remaining live stitches.
steps: After the final decrease round, cut the working yarn leaving a tail about 20 cm long.
Thread the tail through the eye of a blunt yarn needle.
Starting with the next live stitch, pass the yarn needle through each remaining stitch in turn while the stitches are still on the knitting needles.
Slide the threaded stitches off the knitting needles, checking that none were missed.
Pull the tail snugly to close the opening, then take the yarn needle through the centre to the inside of the hat.
Secure the tail on the inside by weaving it through the surrounding stitches.
new_lessons.check: All the live stitches are caught on the yarn and the crown opening is closed without a loose stitch.
new_lessons.watch: A missed live stitch can unravel; if one is left behind, put it back on a knitting needle and thread the tail through it before tightening.

sections.title: Cast on
sections.instructions: Using the 5 mm circular needle and a loose long-tail cast-on, cast on 92 stitches. Leave a tail for weaving in.
sections.tip: Cast on loosely enough for the brim to stretch over your head.

sections.title: Join
sections.instructions: Arrange the stitches around the circular needle without twisting the cast-on edge. Place a marker for the beginning of the round, then join to work in the round.
sections.tip: The cast-on edge should point inward all the way around.

sections.title: Deep folded brim
sections.instructions: Work the 2 × 2 rib in rounds. About 38 rounds are estimated; add or omit rounds as needed to reach the measured length. This brim will be folded in half.
sections.until: The rib measures 16 cm from the cast-on edge, unstretched.
sections.tip: Keep the yarn at the front for purl stitches and at the back for knit stitches. Check that the brim stretches comfortably around your head.

sections.title: Seed-stitch body
sections.instructions: Work the two-round seed-stitch repeat, about 22 times, adjusting by complete repeats to reach the length. The body is deliberately long for a relaxed slouch.
sections.until: The seed-stitch section measures about 15 cm from the top of the rib, unstretched, ending after a complete two-round repeat.
sections.tip: Knit the purl bumps and purl the knit Vs from the round below.

sections.title: Shaped crown
sections.instructions: Work the listed rounds once in order, beginning at the round marker. The first decrease round makes 88 stitches; the later decrease rounds remove 8 stitches each. Change to 5 mm double-pointed needles when the stitches no longer fit comfortably around the circular needle. This smooth knit crown is a small contrast to the seed-stitch body.
sections.until: Complete all 16 shaping rounds; the crown should measure about 6.5 cm from the start of shaping, depending on your row gauge.
sections.tip: The shaping rounds must all be completed even if their measured length differs from the estimate; adjust the seed body beforehand if needed.

sections.title: Close the crown
sections.instructions: Cut the yarn leaving a 20 cm tail. Thread it onto a yarn needle, pass it through the remaining 8 stitches, slide them off the needles, and pull snugly to close. Take the tail inside and secure it.
sections.tip: This gathered closure replaces a bind-off.

sections.title: Finish
sections.instructions: Weave in both tails, gently wash and dry flat, then fold the ribbed brim up by about 8 cm.
sections.tip: Do not stretch the brim while drying.

finishing: Before starting the hat, make a seed-stitch swatch in the round, wash and dry it as you will the hat, and measure over 10 cm. Aim for 18 stitches; change needle size and swatch again if needed, then use the matching size for both circular and double-pointed needles.
Check the brim stretches comfortably over your head before proceeding too far; the rib pulls in when relaxed.
Gather the crown, weave in the tails, wash according to the yarn label and dry flat.
Fold up about 8 cm of the brim. The estimated finished height with the brim folded is about 29.5 cm, depending on your row gauge.
not_checked: The cast-on, untwisted join, switch to double-pointed needles, gathered closure, weaving in and folding are described in words rather than verified as row recipes.
Actual gauge, fabric stretch, fit, yarn amount and finished measurements depend on your yarn and knitting; check the swatch and try the brim.
The row checker verifies stitch counts and that the recipes fit; it does not verify the appearance of the seed texture or the neatness of the crown.
